content: Cetirizine contains a pseudoephedrine component, which necessitates caution when prescribing it to patients with certain medical conditions. For patients with reduced renal function, the initial dose should be lowered to one tablet per day due to their diminished ability to eliminate cetirizine and pseudoephedrine from the body. When Cetirizine is administered alongside other sympathomimetic amines, careful consideration is required because the combined effects on the cardiovascular system could potentially harm the patient. Both cetirizine and pseudoephedrine are primarily excreted through the kidneys. As a result, patients with impaired renal function are at a higher risk of experiencing toxic reactions to this medication. Since elderly individuals are more likely to have reduced renal function, it is important to exercise caution when determining the appropriate dose for this population. Monitoring renal function in these patients may also be beneficial. In elderly patients, dosing should be approached with caution. This is due to the increased likelihood of diminished hepatic, renal, or cardiac function, as well as the presence of other medical conditions or concurrent drug therapies. Cetirizine may impair mental alertness, so patients should exercise caution when driving or operating potentially hazardous machinery. Additionally, the concurrent use of Cetirizine (ZYRTEC) with alcohol or other central nervous system depressants should be avoided, as this combination may further reduce alertness and impair central nervous system performance.
